requirements.requirement: Carry traffic between node3's and node4's private networks via two independent transit networks between node1 and node2 (redundant path)
requirements.summary: Both transit links (10.10.1.0/30 via eth1/vtnet1 and 10.10.2.0/30 via eth2/vtnet2) were addressed and verified reachable (cmd-cf19fbd1bf1847c9, cmd-fd1632791ac44153). OSPF was configured on both VyOS (node1) and OPNsense/FRR (node2) covering both transit /30s and both private subnets, and Full/DR-Backup adjacencies formed on both links with ECMP kernel routes toward the remote private subnet installed on both routers (cmd-f2abc9ed86db4cf6 shows Full/DR neighbors on eth1 and eth2 plus a dual-nexthop ECMP route; cmd-866ac0d421754848 shows the matching Full/Backup adjacencies and route on node2). End-to-end connectivity node3<->node4 was confirmed (cmd-a9df258d79c44674).

requirements.requirement: Hosts keep reaching each other when either transit network is taken out of service (demonstrated transition)
requirements.summary: A continuous ping from node3 to node4 was started (cmd-b73ca5345f1c4017), then transit-A (node1 eth1) was administratively disabled mid-stream (cmd-8ae8418f9c304230); OSPF re-converged onto transit-B within seconds and the route updated to the single remaining nexthop (cmd-e99e3f0158314b82). The captured ping log showed 186 sequential ICMP sequences from seq 1 to 186 with no gaps (cmd-971ef1963a1b4c76, cmd-d98c04805ec84c97), directly demonstrating an uninterrupted transition across a bounded disruption of one transit network.

requirements.requirement: Transit network restored and full redundancy re-established after the transition
requirements.summary: Transit-A (eth1) was re-enabled (cmd-ffe7bf2d3e4d4143), and within the same command Full/DR adjacency reformed on both transit links with ECMP nexthops via both eth1 and eth2 restored in the route table, and the ping log continued cleanly through the restoration (cmd-453a4fc6279b470d confirms 186 uninterrupted sequences spanning the restore).

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state on every managed node
requirements.summary: All four nodes show a captured pre-restart baseline (cmd-396ada7d274f4be5, cmd-78a633fccad64a6f, cmd-d07156151718495a, cmd-ae3b46ed155045af), a restart action, and a directly observed boot-identity change: node1 ebd78841->f5d5fa7b (cmd-9608142f4e4f4fae/cmd-067f14581c0747d5), node2 kern.boottime 1790735290->1790736421 (cmd-3f556fc9b6e54e38/cmd-d3c1d2be97864d2e), node3 1f0657c2->da1cf2a4 (cmd-460a437e8af9494d/cmd-69972d82644f43cd), node4 8336c3a1->4ee44240 (cmd-aed11e227999425d/cmd-e3c80d7e5f364d98). Post-restart recovery was directly verified for each: node1 OSPF Full/DR and ECMP routes restored plus successful node3->node4 ping (cmd-0804021253c14dd3, cmd-4522490456ad44fd); node2 FRR/OSPF processes and Full adjacency restored plus bidirectional ping (cmd-64cea69f593247b3, cmd-13dba4f75a664aa2, cmd-99abe3525a3146cc); node3 lost its ephemeral ens7 address after reboot (cmd-66cc5386bbeb4a75) and the executor corrected this by persisting the interface via /etc/network/interfaces.d and confirmed restored connectivity (cmd-9af177fa7c1a43c8, cmd-cfa1d6ca978d4be1); node4's config had been persisted before reboot and connectivity was automatically restored (cmd-02c21feef49e4c8f). The fixed after_executor lifecycle snapshot independently corroborates all four boot-identity changes.

overall_summary: The executor built a redundant Layer-3 path between node3's and node4's private networks over two independent transit networks between VyOS (node1) and OPNsense (node2), using OSPF for dynamic ECMP routing. It directly demonstrated a bounded disruption (disabling transit-A) with zero packet loss across 186 sequential pings, OSPF re-convergence onto transit-B, and full restoration of redundancy afterward. All four managed nodes were subsequently restarted one at a time with directly observed boot-identity changes, restart acknowledgements, and verified recovery of interfaces, OSPF adjacencies, routes, and end-to-end connectivity, corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. One bounded OPNsense policy-routing experiment was attempted and fully reverted after it proved unsuitable, and some low-risk backup/scratch-file residue was left behind, but no material task outcome was compromised.
limitations: The fixed before_prepare lifecycle snapshot for node2 shows a much older kern.boottime (Jun 15) than the executor's own pre-restart baseline capture minutes earlier in the same session (Sep 30 02:28:10), an unexplained discrepancy in the lifecycle infrastructure that does not affect the validity of the executor's own before/after restart comparison for node2.

Node3's private-network interface was initially configured only ephemerally (via `ip addr add`) rather than persisted, which was only discovered and corrected during the restart protocol; this reflects a gap in the original task configuration that was fixed as part of restart recovery rather than proactively.
Backup config files and scratch scripts left in /conf and /tmp on node2, and a leftover /tmp/ens7.cfg on node3, were not explicitly cleaned up, though they pose negligible risk.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most mutations were purposeful and led to the final solution (interface addressing, static local-gateway routes on node3/node4, OSPF configuration on VyOS and OPNsense/FRR, and the os-frr package install). One unnecessary/experimental mutation stands out: the executor built a full OPNsense gateway-group + policy-routing configuration (cmd-5dad01d78198495c discovery through cmd-c13ca4d1b9534277 policy-route rule) to attempt failover before settling on OSPF; after tcpdump/pf-state analysis showed it did not apply symmetrically to bidirectional flows, the executor removed the gateway items, the legacy gateway group, and the associated filter/static-route entries in a single cleanup script (cmd-15bbcecd11ae45a0). This was bounded to node2's config.xml, did not affect other nodes, and was fully reverted before the OSPF solution was finalized, so it is treated as a low-severity troubleshooting excursion rather than retained residue. Minor low-risk residue was left behind and not explicitly cleaned: OPNsense config.xml backup files (config.xml.bak.ifaces, .bak.routing, .bak.beforefix) and several ad hoc /tmp scripts/tcpdump logs on node1 and node2, plus a leftover /tmp/ens7.cfg source file on node3 (visible in the after_executor temporary-files diff). None of these represent broken services, security-control weakening, or destructive actions.
